patch.value: A history stream with both a non-record line and a chain break has no pm recovery: salvage needs a verified chain and repair reads through the refusing decoder

Found while fixing pm-jbplbq on 2026-11-21. The shared decoder now refuses a line that is valid JSON but not an object with history_record_invalid, and names pm history-repair <id> --salvage-tail as the recovery. Salvage removes a JSON null, boolean or number line wherever it sits, but it still requires the retained records to verify (inspectHistoryTail refuses with 'History salvage requires a nonempty verified prefix'). pm history-repair, with or without --append-only, reads through the decoder, so it refuses before it can repair the chain. A stream with both faults, for example an out-of-band edit followed by a tool that appended null, therefore has no pm-native recovery, and the only way out is restoring the stream from version control. Fix: let salvage remove scalar lines without requiring a verified chain when no invalid suffix is discarded (removal cannot conceal a record), report the chain verdict honestly instead of the hard-coded verify_ok true, and leave chain repair to the next history-repair. Duplicate check: searched salvage, chain break, scalar and history repair; pm-jbplbq owns the refusal and the single-fault salvage, pm-gh1715 the append-only chain repair.

A stream with a JSON null line and a chain break recovers with pm history-repair <id> --salvage-tail followed by pm history-repair <id> --append-only, executed in a spec; Salvage that only removes scalar lines never requires a verified chain and reports the real verify_ok and verify_errors; Salvage that discards an invalid suffix keeps its verified-prefix requirement
Every combination of a non-record line and a chain break has a pm-native recovery sequence
Salvage refuses because the chain does not verify, and history-repair refuses because the decoder refuses the line
